cases.question: What happens if I fail more than 75% of my units?
cases.decision_summary: Preserve both wordings (Section 4.3 more than 75%; table 75% or more). Explain nine-unit condition in its two contexts. Include incomplete-grade exclusion. Distinguish dismissal from the College from permanent disqualification from the University. Flag the exact-75% discrepancy and recommend Registrar confirmation.
cases.draft_reference_answer:
The LSPU Student Handbook 2021 retention policy uses two slightly different failure thresholds.

Section 4.3 states that any student who fails in more than 75% of the total academic units enrolled shall be subject for dismissal from the College. An incomplete grade is not included in the computation of earned units. Section 4.3 also states that this shall not apply to students who receive final grades in only nine academic units.

The scholastic-delinquency table on the following page lists 75% or more, when the student is enrolled in nine academic units or more, as Dismissal from the College (not allowed to enroll). Failing 100% is listed separately as Permanent disqualification from the University, which is not the same as dismissal from the College.

The nine-unit language therefore appears in two contexts: as an exemption in Section 4.3 for students who receive final grades in only nine academic units, and as an enrollment condition in the table (nine academic units or more) for the 75% or more dismissal row.

Because Section 4.3 says “more than 75%” and the table says “75% or more,” these pages do not resolve the exact-75% case. Confirm the applicable rule with the Registrar.

sources.source_section: Undergraduate Academic Policies > Article 5 > Retention Policies > Sec. 4.3 Dismissal
sources.what: Prose threshold, incomplete-grade exclusion, nine-unit exemption
Table rows for 75% or more and 100%

known_ambiguities_conflicts_metadata_dis: Section 4.3: more than 75%. Table: 75% or more. Exact-75% case is unresolved.
Nine units in 4.3 is an exemption (only nine final grades). Nine units in the table is an enrollment condition (nine academic units or more).
Dismissal from the College is not permanent disqualification from the University (100% table row).

cases.decision_summary: Use Faculty Manual 2020 Section III, A. Commitment of Faculty. Concise faithful summary of listed commitments. Do not automatically include B. Code of Ethics. Cite PDF 16-17 / printed 5-6. Record chunk title/page mismatch. Do not modify the knowledge-base chunk.
cases.draft_reference_answer: According to the LSPU Faculty Manual 2020, Section III, A. Commitment of Faculty, faculty commitments include: treating teaching as a personal commitment, including professional maturity, sharing instructional resources, setting aside personal bias, and preparing for quality teaching; placing the learner at the center of the educative process, including respecting students, supporting growth, not ridiculing or condemning them, inspiring their best effort, grading without personal friendship or vested-group pressure, meeting individual needs, encouraging high individual goals, and keeping confidential student information unless required by authorized agency or law; sharing with parents the responsibility of shaping the student’s future, including cooperative relationships and keeping parents informed of academic progress and deficiencies; and serving as a vanguard of change through public service, research, extension, and community engagement.
